hypothesis: During destructive episodes, MTS's many nominally distinct positions become highly exposed to one common market factor, so new entries add redundant systemic risk rather than independent bets.
unit_of_analysis: Underlying ticker, not individual overlapping signal, to avoid mechanically inflating correlation from duplicate exposures.
frozen_metrics: 20-session rolling average pairwise correlation among active underlying tickers with sufficient observations
20-session rolling first-principal-component share of variance among active ticker returns
daily fraction of active tickers negative and absolute deviation from 50 percent
daily new-signal count and unique-entry-ticker count
daily entry redundancy ratio = signals / unique entry tickers
collapse versus control medians and p90 values
primary_interpretation: Support if destructive episodes show materially higher common-factor concentration/co-movement and entry redundancy than temporary-deterioration controls, especially at portfolio troughs. Refute if collapse and control co-movement/concentration are similar.
